segments.text:
V. 25.
Full of rapine and intemperance—The Cenſure is double (taking Intemperance in the vulgar Senſe.) Theſe miſerable Men procured unjuſtly what they uſed intemperately. No wonder Tables ſo furniſhed prove a Snare, as many find by ſad Experience. Thus Luxury puniſhes Fraud, while it feeds Diſeaſe with the Fruits of Injuſtice. But Intemperance in the full Senſe, takes in not only all Kinds of outward Intemperance, particularly, in Eating and Drinking, but all intemperate or immoderate Deſires, whether of Honour, Gain, or ſenſual Pleaſure.
